`appInstallUrl` in `packages/owletto/src/components/connectors/app-install.tsx` (shipped owletto#593).

**Rule:** emit a RELATIVE `/lobu/<provider>/install` path when the SPA and gateway share an origin (prod, `make dev`); an absolute gateway URL only when they differ. Never build it from `API_URL` — that was the bug that made the Install button a no-op on a split host.

Resolution order: `VITE_GATEWAY_URL` → `VITE_API_URL` → `window.location.origin`. Undefined/empty/malformed all degrade to relative (never `undefined/lobu/...`).

**Do NOT "fix" split-origin installs by proxying `/lobu` same-origin.** That was the original workaround. OAuth `redirect_uri`s are registered on the GATEWAY, so routing install through the Vite host breaks the callback. `pi-review` recommends this — it is wrong, and it would regress Slack, which works today.

**`?org=` also cannot fix it.** `resolveRequestedOrgId` (`packages/server/src/gateway/routes/public/install-org.ts`) resolves the slug then gates on `getCachedMembershipRole(orgId, userId)`, and `readUserId` reads ONLY the session context. No cookie → no user → membership check can't run → null. Deliberate: "so a stray `?org=` can't select a foreign tenant."

**The real constraint:** GitHub App install requires an authenticated session on the gateway; split-origin dev deliberately keeps the cookie host-only on localhost. Irreconcilable without authenticating against the remote gateway directly (PAT handoff / sign in on the gateway origin first).

**Slack is NOT affected** — its `oauth-code-exchange` start route explicitly permits a logged-out start and funnels through the claim flow. GitHub's `/github/app/install` hard-401s. Do not generalize a passing Slack test to GitHub; they are different route shapes.

/api/buremba/agents/system-agent -> 401

Your request pattern is byte-for-byte identical to what an anonymous `curl` gets on every one of those endpoints. `/api/auth/get-session` returning `200` with body `null` is the tell — no session. `buremba` is a `private` org, so anonymous → 401 is the middleware behaving correctly (`packages/server/src/workspace/multi-tenant.ts:606-614`, the anonymous fall-through).

- **Stale deploy** — prod runs `84821ec46`, exactly `origin/main` HEAD.
- **Server/DB health** — both `lobu-app` pods 0 restarts, all 200s, no errors in 3h of logs.

## Two real defects this exposed

1. **No auth guard in the SPA.** `get-session` → `200 null` is treated as good enough to render the workspace, so you get "Couldn't load the workspace builder. Authentication required." instead of a redirect to sign-in. The only redirect-on-unauth in `packages/owletto/src` is `app/auth/accept-invitation.tsx`.
2. **`multi-tenant.ts:580` swallows session errors.** A bare `catch {}` converts *any* session-validation failure into "anonymous" with no log line — which is exactly why 87 × 401 produced zero signal in prod logs. This violates the fail-closed-with-a-visible-log invariant in AGENTS.md.

The exact sequence to get a `make task-setup` worktree testable in a browser. Verified 2026-07-29 in `.claude/worktrees/merge-snapshot-evidence` (PORT=9143). Each step below cost a wasted round-trip when skipped.

**1. `make build` is a NO-OP — the target you want is `make build-packages`.**
`make build` prints "Nothing to be done for `build'" and exits 0, which looks like success. A fresh worktree has no `packages/*/dist`, so until you run `make build-packages` vitest dies at import time with `Failed to resolve entry for package "@lobu/pgvector-embedded"` and then `Failed to load url @lobu/core/contracts/interaction-envelope`. Both are the same missing-dist cause wearing different messages. Related: [[reference_worktree_stale_core_dist]], [[reference_empty_worktree_node_modules_resolves_main]].

**2. `make dev` boots ONLY the API.** It runs `packages/server` (`tsx watch src/server.ts`) on the worktree's `.env.local` PORT. It does **not** serve the SPA — `/` and `/index.html` 404 (health reports `"mode":"cloud"`, and in cloud mode the frontend is hosted separately). `packages/owletto/dist/index.html` existing does not change this. Editing server TS is live via tsx watch; no restart needed.

**3. The SPA is a second process — vite — and must use `LOBU_API_PROXY`, not `VITE_API_URL`.**
```
cd packages/owletto && LOBU_API_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<API_PORT> \
  bun run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port <pick a free one>
```
`prodApiProxy()` in `vite.config.ts` same-origin-proxies `/api`, `/oauth`, `/connect` and rewrites Set-Cookie (drops Domain, SameSite=None→Lax) so better-auth sessions work. `VITE_API_URL` does NOT work for auth — the config comments say so explicitly.

**4. The SPA's backend is the ORIGIN. `/lobu` is the Agent API gateway only.**
Setting `VITE_API_URL=.../lobu` yields `GET /lobu/api/auth-config 404` and a "Not signed in" page. Measured on the live server:
```
/api/auth-config       -> 200
/lobu/api/auth-config  -> 404
```
See [[project_embedded_server_lobu_prefix]] — this is the same split, and it bites the SPA config too.

**5. Dev DB is per-branch on 127.0.0.1:5418** (brew postgresql@18), named `lobu_<branch with / and - as _>` — e.g. branch `feat/merge-snapshot-evidence` → `lobu_feat_merge_snapshot_evidence`. Find it with `psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5418 -l`. A fresh one has 1 org (`local-install`), 1 user, 0 events — so an empty Activity page is EXPECTED, not a bug. Agents `lobu-builder` + `owletto-default` are seeded, but `inference_providers` is empty, so chat may not resolve a model (see [[reference_org_provider_needs_base_url]]).

**6. Integration tests** want `lobu_test`, which is also reachable on 5418:
```
cd packages/server && DATABASE_URL="postgres://$USER@127.0.0.1:5418/lobu_test" PGSSLMODE=disable \
  node ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run <path> -t "<name>"
```

**7. To exercise an AGENT-attributed tool call without wiring an LLM** — the useful trick, since the LLM only decides *to call* the tool and everything under test is downstream. Mint a PAT straight into the dev DB (`token = "owl_pat_" + randomBytes(24).toString("base64url")`, `token_hash = sha256(token)` hex, `token_prefix = token.slice(0,12)`, scope `'mcp:read mcp:write mcp:admin'`), then do the MCP streamable-HTTP handshake against `POST /mcp/<orgSlug>`:
`initialize` → read the `mcp-session-id` response header → `notifications/initialized` → `tools/call`. Send `x-lobu-agent-id: <agentId>` on every call. `classifyMutationPrincipal` gives `agentId` precedence over `userId`, so the context resolves to kind `"agent"` and takes the approval-gated branch instead of the human fast path. Skipping the handshake returns `Bad Request: Server not initialized`.

Do NOT sign in / create the local account yourself — that's the user's step.

Done. Everything is committed on `feat/consolidate-auth-guard` in the worktree, not pushed.

## What was broken

`/$owner` was the only owner-level route with no sign-in redirect. Its sibling `$owner/$.tsx` had one, and `OwnerWorkspaceGate` had a third copy — but the org root had none, so it rendered `systemAgentError.message` verbatim. That string is the raw server 401: "Authentication required. Use OAuth or API key." On a subdomain that route *is* the landing page, which is why an expired session hit it first.

The reason a route could ship with no redirect: the `/auth/login` search literal has seven keys and TanStack wants all of them spelled out, so it was hand-copied at **seven** call sites, five of them purely writing `undefined`. There was nothing to reuse — only a literal to copy.

## The change

New `src/lib/sign-in-redirect.ts` — `signInSearch()`, `currentCallbackUrl()`, `useAnonymousSignInRedirect()`. All seven call sites now use it, the three duplicate guards collapse into one, and the guard is applied at the `$owner` layout — the chokepoint every `/{owner}/...` page passes through.

`314 insertions / 92 deletions` across 11 files; the consolidation itself is net-negative, the growth is the two test files.

One deliberate non-change: an outage still renders the error instead of bouncing. A 5xx is not an authz problem, and "please sign in" would misreport it.

## Verification

**red → green in a real browser** (Playwright + Chrome, anonymous, `singleUserMode` forced off to match cloud shape):

- Before: **3/7** — `/local-install` rendered "Couldn't load the workspace builder", i.e. your screenshot. Deep pages already redirected, confirming only the root was unguarded.
- After: **7/7** — `/auth/login?callbackUrl=%2Flocal-install&intent=sign-in`, deep paths preserve their query (`/local-install/activity?tab=runs`), no redirect loop.
- Signed-in flow re-checked separately: org root → builder chat, activity and connectors load. No regression from the layout-level gate.

Unit: 126 files / 1094 tests. `make pre-pr` clean on all 6 gates. Mutation-tested the new tests — 3 of 4 mutations caught.

## Two things you should know

**`make review-fix` was a mixed bag.** It added two genuinely good test cases (a real 401 `resolve_path` handler instead of relying on the MSW catchall, and a 503 outage test covering a branch I'd left untested — that one caught a mutation). But it also stripped the explanatory comments, split a same-module import in two, and reformatted three whole files. I kept the tests and the one real simplification (`!isNotFoundError` is redundant — `isServerError` is 5xx-only), and reverted the rest.

**I caused that reformatting.** I ran `bunx biome check --write` without `--config-path config/biome.config.json`, so it used biome's defaults. `packages/owletto/**` is excluded from that config exactly like `packages/server` — owletto only runs `biome lint src`, never format. 2. `make review` once on the settled HEAD after the PR exists.

The `check-drift` CI gate FAILS until the lobu pointer is an ancestor of owletto/main (i.e. points to the squash SHA, not the pre-merge branch SHA). Pointing at a branch SHA that gets orphaned by squash breaks prod submodule cloning.

**🚨 When the pointer-PR branch has fallen behind lobu main, use `git merge origin/main`, NOT `git rebase`.** Rebase DROPS the pointer commit ("patch contents already upstream") and then a follow-up `--amend` corrupts whatever commit is now at HEAD (swept a `drop_idx` migration + 600-line diff into the pointer commit once; dropped the gate's 2 commits to leave the branch == main another time). Server files of a gate PR are usually "gate-only" (no real conflict) — only the submodule pointer conflicts.

**make review does NOT auto-approve.** A clean 0-bugs/0-blockers verdict leaves the PR at `REVIEW_REQUIRED` (verified: gate #1485 clean but unapproved). The codex-approver needs a manual 👍 on the Codex comment. As the PR author you can't self-approve via GitHub. For admin-authored PRs where CI+pi are green, **`gh pr merge <n> --repo <r> --squash --admin`** bypasses the self-approve gate — the documented pattern ("lobu --admin"). `--admin` also bypasses spurious required-check fails (a pointer-only PR tripping `migrations`, or `pi-review` failing on 1 pre-existing unrelated bug).

**make review verdict can flag REAL bugs in the submodule** — it dereferences the pointer and reviews the owletto diff. Yes — there's a second gap, and `legal-review` is a different case from what I just fixed.

## What's happening

`legal-review` is a **public** org. Anonymously, on that host:

```
/api/legal-review/resolve_path        POST  200   <- public read works
/api/legal-review/public/connectors   GET   200   <- public read works
/api/legal-review/agents/system-agent GET   401   <- builder blocked
/api/legal-review/agents              GET   401
```

The server is **correct here.** Public access is served two ways: an explicit `/api/{org}/public/*` REST namespace, and tool routes that pass `isPublicReadable`. The gate is `canAccessPublicOrgRequest()` (`multi-tenant.ts:180`), and it bails on the first two lines:

```js
if (!requestedToolName) return false;                              // REST routes have no toolName
if (!['POST','PUT','PATCH'].includes(c.req.method)) return false;  // GET can never qualify
```

So the public carve-out covers tool calls only. `agents/system-agent` is a GET REST route — it can never be public-readable, and it shouldn't be: **the workspace builder is an owner concept.**

The bug is that `$owner.tsx` asks for it anyway, regardless of who's looking. Then it renders `systemAgentError.message` verbatim — same unguarded line as before, so the server's authz sentence becomes product copy. You saw the 403 variant; anonymous visitors get the 401 variant.

## The gap I did *not* close

There are three viewer states at the org root, and I only fixed one:

| viewer | org | today |
|---|---|---|
| anonymous | private | → sign-in ✅ just merged |
| authenticated non-member | private | 403 rendered raw ❌ |
| any non-member | **public** | builder attempted → 401/403 raw ❌ ← `legal-review` |

My fix deliberately does not fire on the public case: the public-bootstrap check suppresses the redirect (right — a public org *must* render for signed-out visitors), and for an authenticated non-member `!session` is false. So it falls straight through to the builder error. I fixed the authentication case and left the **authorization** case, which is the same class.

Worth noting the pieces already exist: `useCurrentOrg()` returns `{ isMember, isPublic }`, `PublicOrgJoinBar` already mounts in the shell for exactly this audience, and SSR already injects a `resolvedPath.workspace` for `legal-review`. `$owner.tsx` just never consults any of it.

## One useful side-signal

That 403 is only reachable inside `if (session?.user && session.session)` — it **requires a valid session**. So you're authenticated now, which confirms the earlier diagnosis: the 401 storm was a stale browser session, and re-login cleared it.

owletto #646 merged (squash `c4661c7a`); lobu #2358 repointed at it and verified an ancestor of `owletto/main`. `make review` came back with zero src/test findings (`slop 0`, `simplicity 93`, `tests_adequate: true`) — its one "blocker" was the check-drift sequencing I then performed. CI is re-running; I'll merge when required checks go green.

Fixing this needs a decision I shouldn't make for you: what should a non-member see at a public workspace's root?

They use **different transports**, and only one of them can be checked against the public-read policy.

The public carve-out lives in `canAccessPublicOrgRequest()` (`multi-tenant.ts:180`), and its first two lines are:

```js
if (!requestedToolName) return false;                              // REST routes have no toolName

```

So it can *only* evaluate tool calls — `POST /api/{org}/{tool}` with a JSON body.

- **Activity** reads via `resolve_path` and `manage_operations` (`list_activity`, `list_runs`) — both allow-listed → renders.
- **Connectors** reads via `manage_connections.list` / `manage_catalog.list_catalog`, plus `/api/{org}/public/connectors` → renders.
- **The root** reads `GET /api/{org}/agents/system-agent` — a REST route. It never reaches its handler; the middleware returns the anonymous 401, and `$owner.tsx` prints that sentence as product copy.

## Why the agents list is empty — and the part that's actually a bug

Same cause, but here it's clearly wrong. Live on `legal-review`, anonymous:

```
GET  /api/legal-review/agents                      -> 401 "Authentication required. Use OAuth or API key."
POST /api/legal-review/manage_agents {"action":"list"} -> 200 {"action":"list","agents":[]}
```

// `list`/`get` are org-read-gated in the handler (requireOrgReadAccess);
// the mutating siblings stay owner-admin (OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS).
manage_agents: new Set(["list", "get"]),
```

The server has **already decided** agent list/get is public-readable. The REST route just never consults that decision, because the policy is only reachable through the tool transport.

So I was wrong earlier when I said "the server is correct here." That held for `system-agent` — the builder genuinely is owner-only — but not for the agents list. This is a **transport gap, not a policy gap**: the intended policy is written down, and one of the two doors doesn't check it.

1. **The agents list should just work.** Point the SPA's agent reads at the transport that honors the policy, or teach the REST layer `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS`. The latter fixes the whole class of `/api/{org}/*` REST routes rather than this one instance — which matches the "fix the class, not the instance" rule, though it's the larger change. I'd start by confirming how many other REST routes are in the same position before choosing.

2. **The root shouldn't ask for the builder at all when you're not a member.** There's no public "system agent" concept, so no policy change makes this one work — the org root needs to render the public workspace view instead. That's the piece where I still want your call on what it shows.

# Public workspaces: REST routes don't honour the public-read policy

**Status:** unfixed, not started. Handoff for a fresh agent.
**Repro host:** https://legal-review.lobu.ai (org `legal-review`, visibility `public`)
**Written:** 2026-07-30, against `origin/main` @ `e8b09ad9`

---

## Symptom

On a **public** workspace, some pages render for a non-member and others fail:

| URL | result |
|---|---|
| `legal-review.lobu.ai/activity` | ✅ renders |
| `legal-review.lobu.ai/connectors` | ✅ renders |
| `legal-review.lobu.ai/` (org root) | ❌ "Couldn't load the workspace builder. / You are not a member of this organization" |
| sidebar agents list | ❌ empty |

The error text is the **server's raw authz sentence** printed as product copy (see "Related, already fixed" below — the same render path).

---

## Root cause

The public-read carve-out can only evaluate **tool calls**, never REST routes.

`packages/server/src/workspace/multi-tenant.ts:180` — `canAccessPublicOrgRequest()`:

```js
if (!requestedToolName) return false;                              // REST routes have no toolName param
if (isMcpRoute) return false;
if (!['POST','PUT','PATCH'].includes(c.req.method.toUpperCase())) return false;  // a GET can never qualify
```

Consumed at `multi-tenant.ts:200`:
```js
const allowOrgLevelPublicRead =
  requestedOrgVisibility === 'public' && (await canAccessPublicOrgRequest());
```

When it returns false the request never reaches its handler — the middleware answers with
`multi-tenant.ts:610` (anonymous → 401 `Authentication required. Use OAuth or API key.`) or
`multi-tenant.ts:566` (authenticated non-member → 403 `You are not a member of this organization`).

So: pages that read through `POST /api/{org}/{tool}` work; pages that read through
`GET /api/{org}/...` REST routes do not.

- Activity → `resolve_path`, `manage_operations.list_activity|list_runs` (allow-listed) ✅
- Connectors → `manage_connections.list`, `manage_catalog.list_catalog`, `/api/{org}/public/connectors` ✅
- Agents list → `GET /api/{org}/agents` ❌
- Org root → `GET /api/{org}/agents/system-agent` ❌

---

## The actual bug: same data, two doors, opposite answers

`packages/server/src/auth/tool-access.ts:181` — the policy **already says agent reads are public**:

```js
// `list`/`get` are org-read-gated in the handler (requireOrgReadAccess);
// the mutating siblings stay owner-admin (OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS).
manage_agents: new Set(["list", "get"]),   // inside PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS (declared at :148)
```

Verified live, anonymous, no credentials:

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://legal-review.lobu.ai/api/legal-review/agents
401

$ curl -s -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"action":"list"}' \
    https://legal-review.lobu.ai/api/legal-review/manage_agents
{"action":"list","agents":[]}          # 200
```

**This is a transport gap, not a policy gap.** The intended policy is written down and
enforced on one door; the REST door never consults it.

Full anonymous probe set:
```
/api/legal-review/resolve_path          GET 200  POST 200
/api/legal-review/public/connectors     GET 200
/api/legal-review/manage_agents         POST {"action":"list"} 200
/api/legal-review/agents                GET 401
/api/legal-review/agents/system-agent   GET 401
```

---

## Two sub-problems — fix them separately

### 1. REST routes ignore `PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS` (server) — a real defect

Agent list/get is *supposed* to be publicly readable. Two directions:

- **(a) class fix:** teach the REST layer the same policy, so every `/api/{org}/*` REST route
  that has a public-readable tool equivalent behaves consistently.
  Matches AGENTS.md "fix the class, not the instance". **Do the enumeration first** — count how
  many REST routes are in this position before committing to the shape.
- **(b) instance fix:** point the SPA's agent reads at the tool transport.
  Smaller, no server change, but leaves the next REST route to rediscover this.

Recommend starting with the enumeration, then choosing. Do not assume (a) is small.

### 2. The org root asks for the builder regardless of viewer (frontend) — a product call

`packages/owletto/src/app/$owner.tsx:42` calls `useSystemAgentId()` unconditionally, and
`:110-117` renders `systemAgentError.message` verbatim.

No policy change can make this one work: **the workspace builder is genuinely owner-only** —
there is no public "system agent" concept, and `set_system_agent` is in `OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS`.
The root must stop requesting it for non-members and render the public workspace view instead.

Pieces that already exist and should be reused rather than rebuilt:
- `useCurrentOrg()` → `{ org, isMember, isPublic, isLoading }`
- `PublicOrgJoinBar` — already mounted in `components/shell/responsive-app-shell.tsx` for exactly this audience
- SSR already injects `window.__LOBU_PUBLIC_BOOTSTRAP__` with `resolvedPath.workspace` for public orgs
  (confirmed present on legal-review)
- `resolve_path` already serves the workspace root anonymously

**Open design question for the user:** what exactly a non-member sees at a public workspace root.
Leading proposal: the public workspace view + join CTA for non-members; builder unchanged for members.
Do not implement past this without confirming.

---

## Related, already fixed — do NOT redo

lobu **#2358** (`e8b09ad9`) / owletto **#646** (`c4661c7a`), merged 2026-07-30.

Added `packages/owletto/src/lib/sign-in-redirect.ts` (`signInSearch`, `currentCallbackUrl`,
`useAnonymousSignInRedirect`), consolidated 3 duplicate guards + 7 copies of the 7-key
`/auth/login` search literal, and applied the guard at the `$owner` layout.

That covers **anonymous + private org → redirect to sign-in**. It deliberately does *not* fire here:
- the public-bootstrap check suppresses the redirect (correct — a public org must render signed-out)
- for an authenticated non-member `!session` is false

So the three viewer states at the org root are:

| viewer | org | state |
|---|---|---|
| anonymous | private | ✅ fixed in #2358 |
| authenticated non-member | private | ❌ raw 403 |
| any non-member | **public** | ❌ this document |

An **outage** (5xx) must keep rendering the error rather than bouncing to sign-in — that
distinction is deliberate and covered by a test in `owner-root-redirect.test.tsx`. Preserve it.

---

## Separate follow-up, also unfixed

`packages/server/src/workspace/multi-tenant.ts` — the session block ends in a bare `catch {}`
that silently reinterprets **any** session-validation failure as "anonymous", with no log line.
~87 production 401s produced zero signal in the pod logs because of it. Needs at minimum a
`logger.warn`. Arguably violates the AGENTS.md "fail closed with a visible log" invariant.

---

## Repro

```bash
# public org, no credentials
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://legal-review.lobu.ai/api/legal-review/agents          # 401
curl -s -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"action":"list"}' \
  https://legal-review.lobu.ai/api/legal-review/manage_agents                                          # 200

# confirm the org really is public
kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -c postgres -- \
  psql -U postgres -d owletto -t -A -c \
  "SELECT slug, visibility FROM organization WHERE slug='legal-review';"                               # legal-review|public
```

and refuse `/api/local-init`, or the SPA silently authenticates you.
